title: autotune: improve batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Recent customer signals and internal unit-econ experiments show significant cost savings when conservative defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching are replaced with workload-adaptive defaults plus model-specific quantization profiles. This PR updates autotune defaults, introduces quantization profile metadata, and adds a small unit-econ CLI used by the optimizer and by SRE during sizing exercises.

What this PR does: - Default batching window reduced from 50ms to 25ms for latency-sensitive tiers and increased adaptive max batch size heuristics based on observed sequence length distributions. - Enable KV-prefix caching by default for routes with high prefix reuse and provide a low-overhead sampling path to detect safe cacheability. - Add per-model quantization profile manifests (fp16/int8/awq hints) and a selection pipeline used by the autotuner to recommend profiles based on SLO/cost targets. - Add unit-econ CLI (redwood uecon) that consumes telemetry snapshots and outputs cost/latency tradeoff recommendations; includes JSON and CSV export. - Wire the unit-econ recommendations into the autotune workflow and the console suggestions engine.

Backwards compatibility: All changes are additive; previous explicit configs remain honored. Quantization profiles only apply when a profile is selected by the autotuner or by an explicit model config.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for sampler, quant profile parser, and CLI added. - Integration test added that runs the autotune flow against small synthetic trace and verifies cost delta and no regressions in median latency. - Benchmarked on perf-canary: median latency change within SLO for the latency tier, p95 improved for cost-optimized tier, and observed 12-21% cost reduction on our internal eval workloads.

Rollout plan: staged rollout by customer tier: start with internal perf-canary, then opt-in beta via feature flag for 10 customers, then gradual ramp with telemetry guardrails and a rollback toggle.

Related: references prior autotune work in PRs pr-24790 and pr-24231 and Linear tasks ENG-3124 and ENG-3187.

release_notes:
- Autotune: improved batching defaults and adaptive heuristics.
- Serving: KV-prefix caching enabled by default for cacheable routes with low overhead sampling.
- Models: per-model quantization profile support and selection pipeline.
- Tooling: redwood uecon CLI for unit-econ analysis and CSV/JSON export.
